title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional fallback ordering
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: After a partial regional outage on 2024-11-11 we observed thrashing in the SLO enforcer where multiple simultaneous regional fallbacks could re-order in-flight decisions, causing duplicated load-shedding and unnecessary circuit-breaker toggles. This resulted in higher error budget burn and customer-visible 503s for some long-tail requests. This hotfix makes the regional fallback ordering deterministic and race-resistant by: (1) introducing a stable priority comparator that prefers explicit region affinity, then fallback priority, then enqueued sequence id; (2) wiring a monotonic in-memory sequence id at enqueue time to prevent reordering when concurrent fallback decisions are reconciled; (3) adding a short-term in-flight state migration so controllers reconcile existing requests without losing priority; (4) adding new unit and integration tests that reproduce the thrash scenario; (5) exposing a temporary feature flag (slo_enforcer.stable_fallback_ordering) to toggle the behavior in staging while we monitor metrics. This description includes implementation details, test coverage, and rollout plan. Rollout plan: enable in staging, validate SLO burn/latency for 24h, enable on Dedicated canary region, then globally. Revert path: flip feature flag off to restore prior ordering. Related: ENG-2146, SUP-4121. Checklist: - [x] Repro test that demonstrates reordering/thrashing - [x] Code change with deterministic comparator - [x] Migration to reconcile in-flight entries - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Metrics + tracing hooks added - [x] Feature flag + docs for staging rollout Notes: This is a hotfix intended to be minimal and low-risk; it avoids major refactors of the enforcer scheduling internals and focuses on ordering and reconciliation semantics.
commits: 1) ensure: add stable fallback ordering comparator and monotonic enqueue id; 2) fix: reconcile in-flight enforcer state during migration; 3) test: add unit + integration tests for fallback ordering and thrash scenario; 4) ops: add feature flag and rollout notes; 5) docs: add short note to slo-enforcer README about ordering semantics
